To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
a seizure susceptibility quantitative trait locus on mouse chromosome 1 is associated with a potassium channel gene.

we have confirmed the seizure-related quantitative trait loci of Chr 1 in mice, mapped it to a fine delimited region, and identified a potassium channel gene, Kcnj 10, as a candidate seizure susceptibility gene.
we have identified a seizure susceptibility QTL on mouse chromosome 1 that contains several candidate genes and that one of these, Kcnj 10, is associated with the seizure phenotype in the mouse.

identifying genes that are responsible for differences in susceptibility to seizures among mouse strains.
the identification of genes that influence susceptibility to seizure.
the genetic and molecular basis of seizure susceptibility in mice.

a gene on mouse Chr 6 is associated with seizure susceptibility.

the distal portion of mouse Chr 1 contains a single gene or tightly clustered group of genes that are responsible for a major fraction of the difference in seizure threshold between the two parental strains.
